name: es30-sync-objects
title: Sync objects: fences, client and server waits, flush and finish
summary: Fence sync objects: a two-slot vertex buffer ring rewritten with MAP_UNSYNCHRONIZED_BIT and guarded by fences (every pixel of 16 cells checked), the legal results of glClientWaitSync, glWaitSync with TIMEOUT_IGNORED, glGetSynciv properties, glFlush and glFinish observed through fence status, an asynchronous glReadPixels into a pixel pack buffer polled with a fence, MAX_SERVER_WAIT_TIMEOUT, object lifetime and the errors the specification defines.
spec: ES 3.0 §5.2 Sync Objects and Fences, Table 5.1, §5.2.1 Waiting for Sync Objects, §5.2.2 Signalling
ES 3.0 §6.1.8 Sync Object Queries, Table 6.29 (MAX_SERVER_WAIT_TIMEOUT), §6.1.2 Data Conversions
ES 3.0 §2.10.3 Mapping and Unmapping Buffer Data (MAP_UNSYNCHRONIZED_BIT), §4.3.2 Reading Pixels (pixel pack buffer)
GLSL ES 3.00 §7.1 Vertex Shader Special Variables (gl_VertexID)

api.glFenceSync: fences after every ring update, after heavy draws and 32 back to back; returned names are non-zero, distinct and glIsSync TRUE
api.glClientWaitSync: legal result sets (timeout 0: ALREADY_SIGNALED/TIMEOUT_EXPIRED; 50 ms with flush: loop until signaled, never WAIT_FAILED), ALREADY_SIGNALED for any timeout once signaled including 2^64-1, WAIT_FAILED + INVALID_VALUE for 0 and deleted names, polling guarded readback
api.glWaitSync: TIMEOUT_IGNORED raises no error and the draw queued behind it executes (pixel compared); timeout 0, 1 s and 2^64-2 -> INVALID_VALUE; null and deleted names -> INVALID_VALUE
api.glGetSynciv: OBJECT_TYPE = SYNC_FENCE, SYNC_CONDITION, SYNC_FLAGS = 0, SYNC_STATUS through creation, glFlush, glFinish and waits; bufSize 2 / 0 and a null length; nothing written and INVALID_VALUE for 0 and deleted names
api.glIsSync: TRUE for fences, FALSE for 0 and immediately after glDeleteSync
api.glDeleteSync: unsignaled fences can be deleted (no error, name invalid at once); 0 is ignored; a deleted name -> INVALID_VALUE
api.glFlush: after glFlush a fence of a heavy draw becomes SIGNALED within a bounded poll of glGetSynciv alone
api.glFinish: the fence created just before it is SIGNALED on the first query and glClientWaitSync(0) returns ALREADY_SIGNALED
api.glGetIntegerv: MAX_SERVER_WAIT_TIMEOUT returned clamped to the int range
api.glMapBufferRange: MAP_WRITE_BIT | MAP_UNSYNCHRONIZED_BIT rewrites of the ring buffers (every pixel compared); a read mapping of the pixel pack buffer is compared with the heavy draw's color
api.glUnmapBuffer: returns TRUE for every ring update
api.glBufferData: ring buffers created empty and rewritten; the pixel pack buffer pre-filled with 0xA5 (the negative control)
api.glReadPixels: RGBA / UNSIGNED_BYTE into a pixel pack buffer; the data equals the heavy draw's color once the fence is signaled
api.glDrawArrays: ring rectangles (TRIANGLE_STRIP) and the full-viewport heavy triangle; pixels compared
api.glGenVertexArrays: two ring-slot VAOs and one without attributes
api.glBindVertexArray: VAO switching selects the ring slot drawn
api.glEnableVertexAttribArray: position and color of the ring rectangles; observed through pixels
api.glVertexAttribPointer: position (offset 0) and color (offset 8), stride 20; observed through pixels
api.glUniform1i: u_iterations (loop count of the heavy shader)
api.glUniform1f: u_zero = 0.0 keeps the heavy shader's output exactly u_color
api.glUniform4f: u_color of the heavy draw: the pixel pack buffer and the center pixel equal it

visual_review.notes: Viewed the gpu, llvmpipe and zink es-max captures (256x256, identical; 0/255 deviation in every cell). A 4x4 grid of 64x64 cells on the dark-blue clear color, each holding exactly one axis-aligned rectangle of its own size, position and color (sixteen distinct colors; cell 0, the top left, is a small dim gray square, e.g. cell 3 a mint rectangle near the top edge, cell 11 a red-orange one), no rectangle touches or crosses a cell border, neighbouring cells never repeat a rectangle, and there are no stray marks or leftover pixels from the heavy full-viewport draws that validate() issues (the image is re-rendered at the end).
